sources.title: M602 Fall 2024, Volume 1: Energy method and applications
sources.locator: Part I, Chapter 3, §§3.3 and 3.4.4, Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.5; the notes state that the general Poincare proof is outside their scope.

contents.argument: Independent energy-method treatment multiplies a PDE by the solution, integrates by parts, uses boundary data, and applies Poincare; the local theorem supplies its own residual proof and explicit channel constant.
General energy-method/Poincare context only; it does not state the assigned nonlinear Couette threshold.

sources.title: Fluid Mechanics lecture notes, Chapter 2: The Navier–Stokes Equation
sources.locator: §3.2.2 Couette Flow, printed pp. 64–65/PDF pp. 10–11; Stokes-flow dissipation argument, printed pp. 82–83/PDF pp. 28–29.

contents.argument: The Stokes minimum-dissipation argument is adjacent context, not the assigned residual estimate; no estimate is imported from it.
The full Couette section identifies the linear shear profile and its wall data; the assigned perturbation theorem is proved locally with its own periodic/no-slip hypotheses.

sources.title: Energy stability of plane Couette and Poiseuille flows and Couette paradox

contents.argument: Independent nonlinear energy treatment, but its principal global-decay result is for streamwise perturbations and uses a different dimensionless normalization; it is not the premise or proof of the all-smooth-perturbation sufficient bound authored here.

sources.title: Fluid Mechanics lecture notes, Chapter 4: Instabilities
sources.locator: §5.1 and §5.1.1, printed pp. 182–185/PDF pp. 1–5; the following §5.1.3 discusses the distinct gravity/surface-tension case.

contents.argument: The source derives the potential-flow normal-mode dispersion relation; its equal-density, zero-gravity, zero-surface-tension specialization matches the growth rate after translating its exp(i(kx-omega t)) convention to exp(ikx+lambda t).

sources.title: 6.642 Continuum Electromechanics, Kelvin–Helmholtz Instability
sources.locator: Prof. Markus Zahn, Fall 2008, complete 4-page lecture note; equilibrium, kinematic interface condition, pressure balance, finite-depth dispersion relation, and deep-layer special case.

contents.argument: Independent two-fluid dispersion calculation; taking equal densities, vanishing gravity and surface tension, and the deep-layer limit gives the same positive growth rate for nonzero velocity jump.
